title: Choose the visual world
question: The terminal stays the hero either way. This picks the world around it: the room it sits in, the type, and how the rest of the site reads.

options.label: Black Box, White Cube
options.lineage: contemporary gallery: projection room, then the white cube with wall labels
options.thesis: The hero is the dark projection room. The dive opens onto a quiet white gallery where each system gets a wall and a label.
materials: one projected light: the event horizon
options.viewport: Dark room: name set very large, the terminal centred under it, the black hole low right. Scrolling falls through the horizon and the lights come up on a white wall with About.
options.risk: The dark-to-light change after the dive is a big shift for a site that has always been dark, and it reads as a flash if the transition is not staged slowly.

raised.raise: Catalogue filters re-rank rows in place, keeping each row's identity, and a changed row holds its highlight until you have seen it.
Built work is set solid; design-stage work is set in hairline outline, so status reads before any badge.
Hierarchy by scale contrast alone: no boxed panels and no chips, one display size per room.
Colour stays on hairline edges and live state; every text field stays achromatic.

options.label: Night Monograph
options.lineage: an architecture studio's printed monograph, set on black stock
options.thesis: The site as a studio monograph: full-bleed plates of each system, short captions, a numbered index, and a colophon.
options.viewport: The terminal over the black hole, the name above it in a large grotesk; below the fold, plate 01 runs edge to edge with a two-line caption.
options.risk: This is where most dark developer portfolios land. It is familiar and effective, and familiarity is the cost.

options.label: Bazaar Spread
options.thesis: Case studies as two-page spreads: the screenshot poses on the left, a hairline display headline answers on the right.
options.viewport: A spread: the terminal on the left page, the name in a large hairline display face on the right, the gutter as a fixed seam.
options.case: It fuses well on studio-level finish, but fashion editorial reads as a different world for engineering hiring, and serif display is a familiar AI look.
options.risk: Can feel like a magazine costume on an engineer's site.

options.label: Gate Board
options.lineage: airport departure boards and boarding passes
options.thesis: The catalogue as a departure board ranking systems by status, and each case study as a segmented pass.
options.viewport: The terminal above a live board of systems, each row reranking in place.
options.case: Holds product clarity for the catalogue, but travel ephemera does not say 'engineer' to either audience.
options.risk: Becomes a theme park of split-flap effects if not held to the grid.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: The name as a giant specimen glyph morphing under the pointer.
options.viewport: A single giant letterform with axis sliders.
options.case: Competes with the pinned terminal hero and says nothing about data systems.
options.risk: Type showcase instead of engineering proof.

options.label: Provenance Ribbon
options.thesis: The career as one continuous custody ribbon with gaps and claims.
options.viewport: A red ribbon threading the roles.
options.case: Beautiful for the timeline alone, too narrow for the whole site.
options.kept: Known work set solid, inferred or unbuilt work set in hairline.
options.risk: Archival mood fights a modern studio feel.

options.label: Cloud Edge
options.viewport: A white field with a spectral edge.
options.case: No link to the audience or the work.
options.kept: Colour confined to hairline edges; text fields stay achromatic.

options.label: Cutting Bench
options.thesis: Sections as frames on a perforated rail.
options.viewport: An orange perforated rail across black.
options.case: Orange owning a third of every screen breaks the minimal brief.
options.kept: State shown as a mark, not a hue.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark developer portfolio done at full craft: near-black, Inter, bento grid, soft gradient glow.
canonCard.viewport: The terminal hero, then a bento grid of projects and stats.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from thousands of portfolios by design.
